Kartini.bio: Javanese noblewoman, Raden Ajeng Kartini, whose letters championed girls' education; Indonesia's national heroine for women's emancipation.

Thomas Sankara.bio: Burkinabe revolutionary who led Burkina Faso from 1983 until his assassination in 1987.

Jiddu Krishnamurti.bio: Indian philosopher and speaker on the nature of mind, meditation, and human freedom; rejected all guru roles.

José Rizal.bio: Filipino nationalist whose novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo inspired the Philippine independence movement.

Ernest Hemingway.bio: American novelist known for The Old Man and the Sea and A Farewell to Arms; Nobel Prize in Literature 1954.
Ernest Hemingway.credit: Unknown authorUnknown author or not provided, Public domain

Lee Kuan Yew.bio: Founding father of modern Singapore, prime minister for 31 years and architect of its rise to prosperity.

Oprah Winfrey.bio: American talk-show host and media executive whose long-running show made her one of the most influential broadcasters in history.
Oprah Winfrey.credit: US Embassy South Africa, Public domain

Samuel Beckett.bio: Irish playwright and novelist, author of Waiting for Godot; Nobel Prize in Literature 1969.

J.R.R. Tolkien.bio: English writer and Oxford professor, author of The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings.
J.R.R. Tolkien.credit: Unknown photo studio commissioned by Tolkien's students 1925/6, Public domain

Plato.bio: Greek philosopher, student of Socrates and author of The Republic.

Leo Tolstoy.bio: Russian novelist, author of War and Peace and Anna Karenina.

Thich Nhat Hanh.bio: Vietnamese Buddhist monk and peace activist who popularized mindfulness in the West; nominated for the Nobel Peace Prize by Martin Luther King Jr.

Steve Biko.bio: South African activist who founded the Black Consciousness Movement; he died in police custody in 1977.

Frederick Douglass.bio: American abolitionist and writer who escaped slavery and became a leading voice against it.

Henrik Ibsen.bio: Norwegian playwright, author of A Doll's House; founder of modern drama.

Matsuo Bashō.bio: Japan's most famous haiku master, whose travel journals and spare verses defined the form.

Mencius.bio: Chinese Confucian philosopher whose teachings, collected in the Mencius, argued that human nature is inherently good.

Ban Ki-moon.bio: South Korean diplomat who served as the eighth Secretary-General of the United Nations (2007–2016).

Isaac Newton.bio: English physicist and mathematician who formulated the laws of motion and universal gravitation.

Astrid Lindgren.bio: Swedish author, creator of Pippi Longstocking.

Faiz Ahmed Faiz.bio: Pakistani Urdu poet celebrated for revolutionary verse blending love and political resistance; Lenin Peace Prize laureate.

Edward Said.bio: Palestinian-American scholar who founded postcolonial studies with Orientalism (1978).

François de La Rochefoucauld.bio: French moralist famed for his Maxims on human nature.

Dogen.bio: Founder of the Sōtō school of Zen in Japan and author of the Shōbōgenzō, a landmark of Buddhist philosophy.

Bal Gangadhar Tilak.bio: Indian nationalist leader whose call for swaraj (self-rule) electrified the freedom movement.

Kamo no Chōmei.bio: Japanese poet and essayist whose Hōjōki, written from a tiny hut, meditates on impermanence.

Confucius.bio: Chinese philosopher whose teachings in the Analects shaped East Asian ethics, education, and governance for two millennia.

Abraham Lincoln.bio: 16th president of the United States (1861-1865), who led the country through the Civil War and abolished slavery.

Simone de Beauvoir.bio: French writer and existentialist philosopher, author of The Second Sex.

Blaise Pascal.bio: French mathematician, physicist and philosopher, author of the Pensées.

Benjamin Franklin.bio: American polymath - printer, scientist, diplomat - and a Founding Father of the United States.

Charles Dickens.bio: English novelist and social critic; author of A Christmas Carol, Oliver Twist and Great Expectations.

Franz Kafka.bio: Czech writer, author of The Trial and The Metamorphosis.

John F. Kennedy.bio: 35th president of the United States (1961-1963), assassinated in Dallas.

Mark Twain.bio: American writer (Samuel Clemens) known for Adventures of Huckleberry Finn and The Adventures of Tom Sawyer.

Fyodor Dostoevsky.bio: Russian novelist, author of Crime and Punishment and The Brothers Karamazov.

Desiderius Erasmus.bio: Dutch Renaissance humanist, author of In Praise of Folly.
